note:
SITE A LANDED, SITE B NOT. Measured on M2 Pro darwin/arm64 go1.26.5, 3 reps of -benchtime 300ms, medians: BenchmarkReduceVJPSum 542,915 -> 148,228 ns (3.66x) with BenchmarkReshapeVJPFastF32 as an untouched calibration at +1.9%. The task predicted 4-6x (560 -> 95-140 us); actual 3.66x, just outside the band. ReduceVJPMean shares the code path and measures ~155 us after, but its before was never measured in this session so no ratio is claimed for it.

THE FINDING THAT MATTERS MOST: THE PATH WAS COMPLETELY UNGATED. Mutation-probing the existing suite BEFORE writing any test showed that breaking the strided gather (gs[of+j*s] -> gs[of]) and disabling the outer odometer entirely BOTH left every autograd test green — nothing exercised a non-zero innermost stride or a multi-row odometer through this VJP. A rewrite of an ungated hot loop is exactly where a silent numerical regression lands. The new cross-reference gate holds the strip-mine bit-identical to a frozen copy of the per-element loop across ranks 1-4 and every subset of reduced axes, F64 and F32, and all three mutations now turn it red. A second test pins the fallback contract: a declined shape must return false and leave the destination untouched, because returning true after writing nothing would silently zero every gradient.

NO NEW PERFSCAN RULE WAS MINTED. PS4005 per-element-odometer already flags these exact sites (vjp.go:111, vjp_reduce.go:113/:130) — it was created for this shape in an earlier round, so it is reused rather than duplicated (PROC-014). Its MESSAGE was corrected, though: it claimed bit-identity by construction flat out, which holds only for a STORING loop. For an ACCUMULATING loop the per-destination summation order must be preserved AND a hoisted scalar accumulator must keep the element type — widening to float64 and narrowing once is MORE accurate, hence a different answer. That is precisely what site B turns on, and the rule now says so.

SITE B NOT DONE: bcastSumInto (autograd/vjp.go:111), reached from the OpAdd, OpSub and OpMul VJPs — every bias gradient in every linear layer, so broader reach than site A. It is the accumulating variant, so the element-type constraint above is load-bearing, and it will need its own ungated-path probe first: assume nothing about existing coverage given what site A revealed. BenchmarkBcastReduceBiasF32 drifted 262 -> 279 us across this session while the calibration moved 1.9%; that code is untouched, so the movement is machine drift, and site B needs a fresh before/after taken in one session.

The two retained fallback odometers carry //perfscan:ignore directives, verified effective by re-running the scan (PERF-SUPPRESS-INERT-001). PS4005 tree-wide 6 -> 4.

body:
Research proposed hoisting the per-(token,expert) renormalization quotient out of the d loop in the MoE combine VJP (vjp_moe.go, both dtype arms). The argument was arithmetic and sounded strong: at the fixture (tks=4096, e=8, d=256) the mix loop performs tks*d*e = 8.39M f64 divisions, the M2 Pro FP divider is not pipelined at roughly 7 cycles throughput, and the sibling loop with the same trip count carries no division. Estimated 25 to 50 percent.

IMPLEMENTED AND MEASURED: no win. BenchmarkMoECombineBackward at -benchtime=100x, 6 samples per arm: before median 5.51 ms, after median 5.60 ms. A first round at 20x was too noisy to read at all (spread over 20 percent within one arm), which is itself worth remembering for this benchmark. Reverted.

Why the estimate was wrong: the inner loop gathers es[i][eb+j] across e SEPARATE slices, so each iteration touches a different cache line and the loop is memory-bound, not divide-bound. The divider latency hides behind the loads. Counting arithmetic operations predicts the cost of a loop only when the operands are already resident.

The transform itself is sound and bit-identical (same quotient, same operands, same ascending-i accumulation) — it is simply not worth anything here. If the gather were ever restructured so the expert outputs were contiguous per token, the division would become visible again and this is the first thing to retry.

The companion suggestion from the same research, interchanging to i-outer/j-inner so the e slice headers load once per expert, was not measured separately and remains open.

Acted on two open candidates from the previous rounds research.

SHIPPED. (1) Cholesky VJP: three of the four cubic loops now go through the in-package striped helper logdetParallelIdx; the forward substitution stays serial because column j depends on the columns before it. Disjointness is what makes each bit-identical — row i of P touches only p[i], column j of T only tmpT[j], and iteration i of the S loop writes (i,j) and (j,i) for j>=i, where a clash between two i values would force them equal. BenchmarkCholeskyVJP_256 -66.0 percent (17.17 to 5.84 ms), _512 -71.5 percent (145.3 to 41.4 ms). Compounded with the previous rounds relayout the benchmark has gone 23.3 to 5.8 ms at n=256 and 186.4 to 41.4 ms at n=512. ORDER MATTERED: parallelizing before fixing the layout would have spread a memory-stall problem across twelve cores and hidden it. Race detector clean; GOMAXPROCS=1 passes; the existing bit-identity test now gates the parallel result against the original row-major SERIAL reference and its size sweep straddles the work threshold.

(2) moeParallelTokens claims tokens from an atomic cursor in grains of 16 with per-worker scratch, replacing the equal static split. BenchmarkMoECombineBackward -34.5 percent and -37.4 percent measuring the arms in both orders.

MEASURED AND REVERTED, and this is the useful half. conv1dParallelChannels at grain 8: 126 percent SLOWER. Its body walks the ENTIRE sequence per claim, so a fine grain re-streams the input once per claim rather than once per worker, about 42x the memory traffic; retuned to four claims per worker it was still 8 percent behind the static split, so the static split stays. distillParallelRows at grain 4: -7.4 percent time but +26 percent bytes and +50 percent allocations, because its body allocates softmax scratch per INVOCATION and a cursor invokes it 32 times where the split invoked it 12. Rejected as a trade, not as a transform: it becomes a clean win once the helper carries per-worker scratch the way moeParallelTokens now does. That is the concrete follow-up.

Both conditions are now in the PS3011 advice with their numbers, and the floor asserts they reach the reader, because someone applying that check blindly will make one of exactly these two mistakes.

STILL OPEN: distillParallelRows per-worker scratch then claim; ref SolveSPD substitution closure and stride-k walk; the format/gguf load path, still unmeasurable because BenchmarkReadFileModel skips with no gguf in models/.

The eigh VJP had been named as a candidate for two rounds and skipped both times for the same reason: no benchmark. Writing BenchmarkEighVJP was the whole unblock.

SHIPPED. Two transforms, both already measured on this packages siblings, applied to the kernel that had neither. The final loop formed every (i,j) pair TWICE — at (j,i) its g is this (i,j) gt and vice versa — so half the cubic accumulation was recomputing sums it had already made; computing the upper triangle and mirroring is the same fix that went -34.33 percent on the Cholesky VJP. Separately both operands of the Vt-Vbar inner product were read down a column of a slice-of-slices, so transposed copies make each inner loop walk two contiguous runs. BenchmarkEighVJP_128 -32.4 percent, _256 -33.9 percent. Trade: two extra n-by-n intermediates, 670446 to 938984 B/op and 522 to 780 allocs at n=128.

THE BENCHMARK KEEPS THE EIGENVALUES WELL SEPARATED ON PURPOSE. The rule divides by (w_j - w_i), so a near-degenerate spectrum would benchmark a numerically different path from the one real callers take.

GATE: TestEighVJPTriangleAndLayoutAreBitIdentical holds the original nest verbatim and compares raw bits across n in 1,2,3,7,16,33 — the degenerate triangles at 1 and 2, and an odd n so the mirror is exercised off a square boundary. Reversing the symmetric add stays GREEN, which is correct and is exactly the property that licenses the triangle; a wrong mirror index reddens it.

CHECK ADDED: PS3031 symmetric-pair-computed-twice. THE FIRST DRAFT WAS IMPRECISE AND THE COUNT SAID SO: requiring only the mirrored pair of accumulations gave 27 findings, and the ones read were unrolled GEMM bands and convolution taps that merely look mirrored because renaming two loop variables makes two unrelated terms render identically. Requiring that both accumulators feed ONE ADDITION — the symmetric store, which is what makes the mirror free rather than load-bearing — took it to 1 pre-fix and 0 after. Recorded because the failure mode is instructive: a syntactic mirror is not a semantic one, and the store is where the semantics live.

STILL OPEN: gguf largest-first tensor claiming (needs a skewed-size benchmark), ReadRaw per-tensor copy (no benchmark), vjp_cv poolAccessors per-element closures (no benchmark), the ref QR and SVD column walks (no benchmarks). Every one of these is blocked on instrumentation rather than on analysis, which is now the dominant constraint on this campaign.

Third round in a row where writing the missing benchmark was the unblock.

SHIPPED. Both pooling VJPs read and wrote every element through closures returned by poolAccessors — one indirect call per read and per write, the AtF64 anti-pattern one level shallower. Typed F64 and F32 arms now walk raw contiguous storage; the closure path stays as the exotic-dtype fallback with character-for-character identical routing. MaxPool2DBackward F64 -48.2 percent and F32 -50.7 percent; AvgPool2DBackward F64 -52.1 percent and F32 -53.2 percent. The four benchmarks are new; this candidate was named two rounds ago and skipped twice for want of one.

THE GATE FOUND A REAL DIVERGENCE. In the typed avg-pool arm the scale product and the accumulating add sit in the SAME function, so Go fused them into an FMA — it may fuse across statements — while in the accessor path the add lives inside a closure and cannot be contracted with the multiply. The typed arm drifted one ulp on elements several overlapping windows accumulate into. An explicit conversion forces the rounding; removing it reddens the test. THE CLOSURE BOUNDARY WAS ACTING AS AN FMA BARRIER, which is a general consequence of devirtualizing anything.

THE FIRST FIXTURE WAS BLIND TO TWO THINGS AND MUTATION SAID SO BEFORE THE CODE DID. With k=2 stride 2 no input element receives more than one accumulation, so 0+gv narrows identically whether the add is done in f32 or widened first — a mutation accumulating in f32 PASSED. And a NaN in x does not reach the max fallback at all: the window max is then simply the largest non-NaN element and the equality search finds it, so a mutation deleting the fallback also PASSED. Overlapping windows (k=3 stride 1) and a NaN in Y fixed both, and only then did either mutation redden — and only then did the FMA divergence appear.

CHECK ADDED: PS3032 closure-accessor-in-loop. No existing check saw this class; the pre-fix site reported only PS6004. Its suppression is unusual and load-bearing: the APPLIED FORM KEEPS THE CLOSURE LOOP as a fallback, so a function that already exits through a guarded fast path must go quiet or the check files its own remedy as the defect. 1 finding pre-fix, 0 after, 36 advisory elsewhere.

STILL OPEN: gguf largest-first claiming (needs a skewed-size benchmark), ReadRaw per-tensor copy, the ref QR and SVD column walks — all blocked on instrumentation.

THE FIRST ATTEMPT WAS THE OTHER FIX AND IT WAS WORSE ON EVERY AXIS. Transposing the column-walked operands — the remedy that paid on the Cholesky, eigh and SVD kernels — gave only -7.3 percent and -12.6 percent and cost 38 percent more bytes (444779 to 613995) and 195 more allocations, because the transposes are extra n-by-m intermediates. Interchange gives three times the win for nothing.

THE DISCRIMINATOR, now in the PS1010 advice and as rule INTERCHANGE-BEFORE-TRANSPOSE-001: whether the loop carrying the strided index is INDEPENDENT. If it merely accumulates it can move outermost and no copy is needed at all; transpose only when that loop cannot move. That is exactly why the three earlier kernels needed copies and this one did not — their strided reads were inside loops whose order the recurrence fixed.

SHIPPED. The SVD backwards tall-matrix correction rebuilt the projection row (W minus U times (Ut W))[i] INSIDE the j loop, n times over, making that term O(m n^3) where O(m n^2) suffices. Hoisting deletes a factor of n of arithmetic — algorithmic, not locality — and the measured ratio grows with size exactly as that predicts: BenchmarkSVDVJP_128x64 -93.4 percent (15.2x), _256x128 -96.5 percent (28.5x). matTmulRect was interchanged in the same commit (contraction index outermost, no memory cost). Both benchmarks are new, sized past L1, and STRICTLY TALL because the correction only runs for m>n — a square cell would have skipped the most expensive loop in the rule entirely.

body:
Question: Can a compile-time darwin/arm64 guard retain all six method-sized VJP bounds-proof hot loops while emitting the original non-target implementations under pinned Go 1.27.1? This is design preflight, not performance qualification or permission to promote either rejected candidate.

Baseline: clean main 14fa6d015fa2482eb5926f03013b976aadda1a09. autograd/vjp_elementwise.go SHA-256 07adbf223e44d862d5f9e3e38a743eff54def329280bb8b76aa0ffe3f9b62945; frozen oracle autograd/vjp_bounds_internal_test.go SHA-256 bd26d0195b02e23aa1406f01f7df25fff5aa65ea81fea0c3bae9f31d3359648c. Prior six-loop source commit 33ca653b/runtime 9969389c is rejected: M2 default/SIMD/race and all six BCE proofs passed, but native default AMD64 Linux/Windows changed 17 sigmoid F64 NaN-payload cases per job. The earlier eight-loop tanh-race failure stays rejected too. Preserve the full six-loop target; do not silently drop sigmoid, relax bits, or rebench rejected code.

Architecture context: LOOP.md states the old design prompt is retired and current Spectackle contracts are authoritative. ADR-0006 fixes the tape/VJP registry boundary; ADR-0005 provides precedent for architecture-gated pure-Go optimization and reference fallback (its old Go1.26 archsimd availability notes are historical, not current capability evidence). Public APIs, registry wiring, backend imports, tests, arithmetic expressions, allocation behavior, tanhVJP, callback order, short-input panic semantics, and generic dtype/layout fallbacks are frozen.

Exact bounded experiment in a fresh isolated detached worktree only: reconstruct the six-loop source from the committed inert evidence patch internal/benchcompare/leadership/evidence/m2-autograd-sixloop-bce-20260910/six-loop-candidate-rejected.diff using apply_patch, checking exact source hash 9969389c before the new variation. Then add the standard runtime import and a single unexported constant darwinARM64VJPBounds = runtime.GOOS == "darwin" && runtime.GOARCH == "arm64" above (not within) existing declaration doc comments. Prefix exactly six original n>=0 length guards with that constant. Do not change any per-element expression, cold fallback body, function signature, helper split, test, compiler flag policy, build tag, or other production file. Keep all speculative source only in the research worktree; root primary branch accepts reports/evidence only at this stage. If this one design fails, report it, do not improvise variants.

Use SDK /private/tmp/goai-go1271-j1cLvq/go/bin/go with PATH prefixed by that bin, GOCACHE=/private/tmp/gocache-goai, GOMODCACHE=/private/tmp/goai-go1271-j1cLvq/modcache, GOTOOLCHAIN=local, GOPROXY=direct, GOFLAGS empty, and GOEXPERIMENT explicitly empty or simd. No package/tool updates. Record GOOS/GOARCH/GOAMD64/GOARM64, CGO, SDK/compiler hashes, all argv/cwd, complete separate stdout/stderr, numeric exit statuses, and artifact hashes. Do not use a shell variable named status (zsh read-only); use task_rc and set -e or explicit exit checking. Preserve failed helper outputs and distinguish script errors from source/test failures.

VERIFY: (1) Before edits, default and SIMD CGO0 go test -short -count=1 ./autograd ./backend/cpu ./nn, plus CGO1 default go test -race -count=1 ./autograd -run ^TestUnaryVJPBoundsExact$. (2) After the guarded variant, repeat those exact commands and CGO1 default go test -short -count=1 ./autograd. Test output must show actual packages, not a filtered pipeline. No paired timing, benchmark, profiler, or speedup claims in this preflight. (3) Build optimized baseline and variant test binaries with go test -c for native darwin/arm64 and cross-target linux/amd64 and windows/amd64 in default and SIMD CGO0 modes. A cross-compile is NOT a native correctness pass. Keep normal optimization on; use -gcflags=github.com/jxsl13/goai/autograd=-d=ssa/check_bce/debug=1 for dedicated diagnostic builds only. Capture full go tool objdump for github.com/jxsl13/goai/autograd.(unaryVJP|reluVJP|sigmoidVJP), including every emitted unary closure clone. Compare exact instruction semantics/control flow between old and guarded variant on both AMD64 OS targets: ignore only source line/path stamps and relocatable absolute addresses; map intra-function branch targets to instruction indices, preserve stack sizes, loads/stores, registers, arithmetic operands, branch directions and call symbols. Do not delete whole lines or numeric immediates to manufacture equality. If PC-relative constant/data references prevent proof, retain them and report inconclusive. Compiler -S output with symbolic relocations may supplement the binary audit. (4) For M2 variant, inspect all six actual hot loop control-flow spans and expected cold fallback checks; source-line-only absence of panicBounds is not enough. Record whether the compile-time guard disappears. (5) Confirm full tanh declaration and oracle bytes unchanged, and no source edits outside the single permitted file.

Deliver one concise REPORT.md plus complete raw captures and exact experimental diff in a new /private/tmp directory, without compiled binaries in Git. Report eligible-for-new-proposal, refuted, or inconclusive, with bounded factual reasons. Even a positive result does not authorize promotion: a subsequent separate implementation task must add actual native strict SIMD test execution to CI (current soft lanes test primitives/KAN/accuracy, not the strict autograd oracle), pass native ARM64/AMD64 default/SIMD/race gates, receive fresh independent verification, and satisfy the unchanged three alternating seven-pair campaign requirements (direct ReLU >=1.05x, taped ReLU >=1.03x, p<0.05, zero allocation increases, no reproducible control regressions >3%, spread near5%).
